question: What is the main objective of the AI Engineer Technical Assessment?
expected_answer: The objective is to evaluate whether an AI Engineer can independently design, develop, test, and deploy an end-to-end intelligent application covering LLMs, RAG, LangChain/LangGraph, AI agents, embeddings, vector databases, prompt engineering, model evaluation, Python/backend engineering, AI architecture, and production deployment.
notes: Section 1 Assessment Objective on page 1.

question: Which file formats must Module A Document Intelligence support for uploads?
expected_answer: Module A Document Intelligence must support PDF, TXT, Markdown, and CSV uploads.
notes: Module A requirements on page 2.

question: What retrieval improvements are listed as options in Module B Advanced RAG Architecture?
expected_answer: Module B lists hybrid search, reranking, query rewriting, metadata filtering, or contextual retrieval as retrieval improvements.
notes: Module B retrieval improvement options on page 2.

question: What capabilities must Module C LLM Integration implement alongside integrating multiple LLM models or providers?
expected_answer: Module C requires structured output, prompt templates, model selection, token tracking, error handling, rate-limit handling, model fallback, and response validation.
notes: Module C requirements on page 2.

question: What are the three required functional tools for the AI Agent in Module D?
expected_answer: The three required tools in Module D are Knowledge Base Search, Document Analysis, and Structured Report Generation.
notes: Module D agent tools on page 2.

question: What features must Module F Application Dashboard provide for authentication, interface, and observability?
expected_answer: Module F requires user authentication, protected routes, dashboard and usage statistics, document management, an AI chat interface, source references, conversation history, agent execution visibility, token usage, latency, errors, and activity logs.
notes: Module F requirements on page 2.

question: What requirements apply to Module E Conversational Memory?
expected_answer: Module E requires supporting multiple conversations and user-specific conversation history, retaining relevant context for follow-up questions, implementing context management to avoid sending unnecessary historical information, and demonstrating a follow-up question referencing previously discussed documents.
notes: Module E requirements on page 2.

question: According to Section 11 Final Expectations, what engineering skills is the assessment looking for?
expected_answer: The assessment looks for an engineer who can design intelligent AI architectures, understand LLMs and their limitations, develop advanced RAG pipelines, build reliable AI agents, integrate external models and tools, evaluate AI output quality, debug complex engineering problems, and deploy production-ready AI applications.
notes: Section 11 Final Expectations on page 5.

question: How do Module B RAG requirements align with Advanced Engineering Challenges 2, 3, and 4?
expected_answer: Module B requires context-aware citations, handling insufficient or conflicting evidence, and retrieval improvements such as hybrid search or reranking, which align directly with Challenge 2 (Prompt Injection Protection treating retrieved content as untrusted), Challenge 3 (Retrieval Optimization via hybrid search, reranking, or query rewriting), and Challenge 4 (AI Response Verification checking that answers are supported by sources).
notes: Cross-page synthesis between Module B (page 2) and Challenges 2-4 (page 3).

question: Contrast the rules for using AI coding assistants during take-home development versus during supervised live technical evaluation.
expected_answer: Under Rule 2, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other AI coding assistants are allowed during development provided the candidate discloses tools used, delegated tasks, independent decisions, identified errors, and code validation. Under Rule 3, AI coding agents and external assistance are prohibited during the supervised live evaluation, and screen sharing is required.
notes: Combines Rule 2 and Rule 3 across chunks 18-19 on page 4.

question: Summarize all AI Evaluation requirements from Module G and the corresponding submission deliverables from Section 9.
expected_answer: Module G requires an evaluation dataset of at least 20 questions covering retrieval relevance, answer correctness, source grounding, hallucination handling, response latency, and token consumption using RAGAS, DeepEval, LangSmith, or a custom framework, along with explaining methodology and limitations. Section 9 requires submitting both the evaluation dataset (>=20 questions) and an evaluation report documenting results, methodology, and limitations.
notes: Multi-page span across pages 2, 3, and 5.

question: How do Module D agent requirements, Challenge 7 Agent Reliability, and Section 8 Live Verification address agent robustness and extensibility?
expected_answer: Module D requires parameter validation, multi-step workflows, failure handling, and at least three tools; Challenge 7 Agent Reliability adds execution limits, parameter validation, timeouts, and recovery mechanisms; Section 8 tests extensibility by requiring candidates to implement a new tool in the existing agent architecture during live verification.
notes: Links Module D (p.2), Challenge 7 (p.3), and Live Verification (p.4).

question: What practices are prohibited under Rule 6 No Fabricated Functionality, and what deployment and credential rules apply to the final submission?
expected_answer: Rule 6 forbids hardcoded LLM responses, mock search presented as real retrieval, fake tool execution, non-functional integrations, screenshots as deployment proof, and fabricated evaluation results. Section 6 and Rule 9/Submission requirements stipulate a live cloud deployment (local-only applications do not qualify) and forbid committing API keys, passwords, or private credentials, requiring a sanitized .env.example file instead.
notes: Combines deployment constraint (p.4), Rule 6 (p.4), and credential security (p.5).

question: Which technologies are suggested in Section 5 for embeddings, vector databases, relational databases, and evaluation?
expected_answer: Section 5 suggests OpenAI or Hugging Face for embeddings, Pinecone or pgvector for vector databases, PostgreSQL or Supabase for relational databases, and RAGAS or DeepEval for evaluation.
notes: Table extraction from Section 5 on page 3.

question: What is the expected duration of the take-home assessment and how long does the mandatory supervised live verification last?
expected_answer: The take-home assessment has an expected duration of 24 hours, and the supervised live technical verification lasts approximately 60 minutes.
notes: Cross-page numerical lookup (24 hours on p.1, 60 minutes on p.4).

question: At least how many questions must the evaluation dataset contain in Module G?
expected_answer: The evaluation dataset must contain at least 20 questions.
notes: Numerical minimum dataset size.

question: How many Advanced Engineering Challenges must a candidate complete out of the total number listed in Section 4?
expected_answer: A candidate must complete at least 3 challenges out of the 7 listed in Section 4.
notes: At least THREE challenges (chunk 11) out of 7 numbered challenges (chunk 13).

question: What are the minimum numbers of LLM providers or models in Module C and functional tools in Module D?
expected_answer: Module C requires integrating at least 2 LLM models or providers, and Module D requires building an agent with at least 3 functional tools.
notes: Numerical constraints inside chunk 7 on page 2.

question: What is the required duration range for the walkthrough demo recording in Section 9?
expected_answer: The demo recording must be a 5 to 10 minute walkthrough.
notes: Numerical duration range on page 5.

question: What example employee query is presented in Section 2 Business Scenario?
expected_answer: Section 2 gives the example query asking to analyze internal technical documentation, identify the most common reasons for system failures, provide evidence from the documents, and recommend possible solutions.
notes: Business scenario example query on page 1.

question: What tasks can be introduced during Section 8 Mandatory Live Technical Verification?
expected_answer: Live verification tasks include introducing a secondary LLM provider with automatic fallback, handling conflicting information from two documents in RAG, implementing a new agent tool, preventing duplicate document-processing jobs, fixing unsupported answers when retrieval returns irrelevant documents, and fixing a security vulnerability in an existing API.
notes: Live technical verification tasks on page 4.
